ryan: hey all — i'm ryan (just started today). trying to build the runtime from source on ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, getting linker errors. any pointers?

paige: welcome ryan! can you paste the linker error and the output of `nvidia-smi` + `nvcc --version`? also which branch you built from?

ryan: thanks! branch is main. error is:
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/lib/libruntime.a(gpu_ops.o): in function `init_cublaslt':
gpu_ops.o:(.text+0x1f4): undefined reference to `cublasLtCreate'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
`nvidia-smi` shows: `Driver Version: 535.86.10`, GPUs: A100.
`nvcc --version` -> `Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105`

jamal: that undefined reference is usually a link-time issue — either the cublasLt lib isn't on the link line or the runtime is picking up a different CUDA install at link vs run. Are you building inside a container?

ryan: building on a dev host (not container). i installed CUDA toolkit via runfile to /usr/local/cuda-12.1 and also have apt-packaged nvidia driver.

talia: common pitfalls: 1) missing `-lcublasLt` or wrong library order; 2) /usr/local/cuda symlink points to a different version; 3) LD_LIBRARY_PATH not configured when running ld. Try: `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` and `ls -l /usr/local/cuda`

jamal: also check pkgconfig or cmake output — ensure target_link_libraries includes cublasLt after your objects. If using our top-level build, try `cmake -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1 ..` and rebuild. Another quick test: link with `-Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 -L/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 -lcublasLt`

paige: one more thing — CUPTI can sometimes cause silent mismatches during profiling link stages. Are you enabling profiling or building with `-DENABLE_PROFILING=ON`? If so, make sure `libcupti.so` from the same toolkit is available.

ryan: ooh i did set ENABLE_PROFILING=ON to debug perf. `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` shows nothing. `/usr/local/cuda` is a symlink to `/usr/local/cuda-12.1` though.

talia: if ldconfig doesn't show it, the toolkit libs might not be in /etc/ld.so.conf.d. Add a file like `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf` with `/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64` and run `sudo ldconfig`.

infra-bot: FYI: we also publish a prebuilt dev image `redwood/dev-runtime:cuda-12.1` with toolchain + drivers pinned. Use `docker run --gpus all -it redwood/dev-runtime:cuda-12.1 /bin/bash` if you want to avoid host-toolkit mismatches.

jamal: if you want a faster workaround while we triage, set `-DUSE_CUBLASLT=OFF` in the cmake to skip cublasLt path (may slightly degrade perf for certain ops). Otherwise, after `ldconfig` confirm with `ldd build/bin/runtime_binary | grep cublas` to see what the linker picks up.

ryan: thanks — i added the ld config and ran `sudo ldconfig`. now `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` shows entries. rebuilding now.

ryan: rebuild succeeded! thanks so much for the quick help. i'll switch profiling off while building locally and use the dev image for future onboarding. :tada:

paige: awesome, welcome aboard again :wave: ping us if anything else pops up.

talia: adding a short checklist to the onboarding doc: ensure /usr/local/cuda-<ver>/lib64 in ldconfig, test `ldd` on binaries, use our dev image for consistent env.

ryan: noted — i'll write up the exact steps i took and drop a PR to docs later.
